title: You want the cross… but you don’t want the story that made it necessary.
paragraphs: You want the cross… but you don’t want the story that made it necessary.

Because that tension right there—
that discomfort—
that quiet resistance in your chest…
That’s where truth begins to break in.

You love the idea of Jesus.
The mercy.
The forgiveness.
The hope.

But the moment the Old Testament opens—
blood.
judgment.
fire.
Because it exposes something we try to hide:

Sin is not small.
And neither is God.
Let me pull you in closer.

The Old Testament is not a random collection of ancient stories.
It is a mirror… and a warning.
It shows humanity at its rawest:

People who saw miracles—
and still chose idols.

People who heard God’s voice—
and still chose rebellion.

People who were rescued—
and still walked back into chains.

We want grace…
without confronting guilt.

We want healing…
without admitting the wound.

We want Jesus as Savior…
but not as Lord.

So we skip the parts of Scripture that feel heavy.
We avoid the Law.
We soften the judgment.
we reshape God into someone we’re comfortable with.

A God who never judges
is a God who never truly saves.

Because if sin is not serious…
then the cross is not necessary.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes the polished version of you.
The disciplined version.
The church-going version.
And the Old Testament doesn’t hide that—it proves it.
“The wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23

And what it earns…
is death.

Spiritual separation.
Judgment.
Distance from a holy God.
The sacrifices in the Old Testament make sense.

The lambs.
The blood.
The altar.
Even those sacrifices were never enough.
“It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.” — Hebrews 10:4

Why all the blood?
Why all the law?
Why all the judgment?

Not as a teacher only.
Not as an example only.
“Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” — John 1:29

Every lamb in the Old Testament…
was pointing to Him.

Every sacrifice…
was whispering His name.

Every drop of blood…
was preparing the world for His cross.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you cleaned yourself up.
While you were still a sinner.
The Old Testament shows you the depth of your sin.
The cross shows you the depth of His love.

So let me ask you—
not casually…
but honestly:
Are you avoiding the parts of God that confront you?

Are you silencing truth…
so you can stay comfortable?

Because partial truth
creates shallow faith.

And shallow faith
cannot carry you through real life.
God is not asking you to be perfect.
He is calling you to be honest.

To see your sin clearly.
To feel its weight fully.
And then—

It is the moment you stop pretending…
and start surrendering.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
Because when you finally see how deep the problem is—

you will finally understand
how powerful the cross really is.
Jesus didn’t come to decorate your life.

But redemption only matters
when you realize you were lost.

And run to the only One
who can carry your sin without crushing your soul.
And if this pierced something deep in you—
Come back to it. Let it work in you.
